thought.text:
I need to distinguish `KEY= #comment` (whitespace before `#`) from `KEY=#literal` (no whitespace). The `_equal_sign` regex `=[^\S\r\n]*` greedily consumes the whitespace, losing that information. I'll capture whether whitespace followed the `=` by peeking before consuming, and pass that to `parse_value`.

The cleanest minimal approach: in `parse_binding`, after reading `_equal_sign`, check if the character immediately after `=` was whitespace. But `_equal_sign` already consumed it. Instead, I can peek at the raw string before reading `_equal_sign`.

Let me restructure: read the `=` char, then peek whether whitespace follows, then read the whitespace, then decide.
